1

Reading · why food tastes better somewhere else

1.1 Discuss. What is the best meal you have ever eaten? Where were you, and who were you with?

KEY WORDS

to rate to judge how good something is

surroundings the place around you

to recall to remember

an ingredient one of the things in a dish

The Best Meal I Never Ate

Ask anybody about the best meal of their life and you will rarely hear about an expensive restaurant. You will hear about a bowl of soup in a bus station, a grilled fish on a beach, something a grandmother made on a cold afternoon. The food itself was almost certainly not the finest they have ever eaten. Something else was doing the work.

Researchers who study taste have measured this repeatedly. The same dish is rated as tastier when it is eaten with other people, when the eater is hungrier, and when the surroundings are unfamiliar. Hunger is the strongest single factor: an ordinary sandwich after four hours of walking really is more delicious than the same sandwich at your desk. Your tongue is not being fooled — hunger genuinely changes how sweet and how salty things taste.

Memory then makes things worse, or better. Every time you recall a meal you rebuild it slightly, and the version you rebuild is a little more perfect than the last one. This is why the cheap restaurant you loved as a student is almost always a disappointment when you go back twenty years later. The restaurant has not got worse. Your memory of it has got better.

None of this is an argument against good cooking. It is an argument against believing that taste lives entirely inside the food. The most reliable way to improve a meal is not a more expensive ingredient but a longer walk beforehand — and somebody to eat it with.

2

Grammar · comparatives and superlatives

PRESENTATION

Short adjectives (one syllable, or two ending in -y): cheap → cheaper → the cheapest · easy → easier → the easiest

Long adjectives (two syllables or more): expensive → more expensive → the most expensive

Irregular: good → better → the best · bad → worse → the worst · far → further → the furthest

Making it stronger or weaker: much / far / a lot cheaper · slightly / a bit cheaper · not nearly as good as

Comparative — two things

Superlative — one out of a group

Curry is spicier than soup.

It's the spiciest dish on the menu.

This café is more expensive than that one.

It's the most expensive café in town.

The machine meal was better than he expected.

It was the best vending-machine meal he'd had.

My cooking isn't as good as yours.

Hers is by far the worst I've tasted.

ERROR WARNING

Never use more with a short comparative, and never use very with a comparative:

more easier ✗ easier ✓ · more big ✗ bigger ✓ · It's very cheaper ✗ It's much cheaper ✓

Superlatives take the, and long adjectives take most, not more:

It was best day ✗ the best day ✓ · the more beautiful city ✗ the most beautiful city ✓ · the most kind person ✗ the kindest person ✓

Word order and spelling: a cupboard bigger ✗ a bigger cupboard ✓ · easyer · thiner · bigest ✗ easier · thinner · biggest ✓

PLAN

Opening — name the place and give your overall verdict in one sentence.

Middle — three of the six areas above. Give one detail for each, not just an adjective.

Balance — one thing that was not perfect, softened: a bit · fairly · not very. Closing — a recommendation: Well worth a visit if…

5.9 Read the model review. Then answer the questions below it.

MODEL

Sabina's, Chilanzar — worth the walk

Sabina's is a small family café behind the market, and it is by far the best lunch I have found in this part of the city. The dining room is fairly plain — six tables, no music — but it is spotlessly clean and the staff are extremely friendly. They serve traditional food, and the lagman is absolutely delicious: the broth is rich, the noodles are made that morning, and the portions are much bigger than you expect. My only complaint is that the place gets a bit crowded after one o'clock, and on my second visit the bread was slightly overcooked. At 35,000 so'm for two people, though, nothing else nearby comes close on value. Well worth a visit if you can get there early.
